description:
## Goal
Make type declaration publication have one explicit source ownership rule. A failed source must neither overwrite nor leave its declaration visible under another source's surviving claim. This is a prerequisite to accepting fz-tfn.46's shared failure-ownership contract.

## Policy decision required
CodeSubmission contains only name/text. CodeMap::define always appends a fresh CodeId; names are display labels, not replacement keys. Existing fz-kdt.24 and fz-kdt.30 require rejecting distinct source owners, and .30 explicitly says another submit_code is not authorized module reopening. No type-specific rule currently decides whether even equivalent duplicate declarations are rejected or may co-own. Recommended contract for confirmation: distinct sources cannot redeclare the same TypeName, even with equivalent bodies; legitimate edits use explicit replacement of a particular existing source, while the same publisher may reevaluate normally. Do not infer replacement from filename, CodeId ordering or job completion order.

Local Elixir reference: ../elixir/lib/elixir/lib/kernel/typespec.ex::collect_defined_type_pairs rejects a repeated name/arity before comparing type bodies. This supports the recommendation, not authority to change Fz semantics without confirmation.

## Evidence
On the uncommitted fz-tfn.46 candidate above e616d82d13cc4e916bfae8e5a48e5219ac680d8a, TypeDeclared(TypeName) now exposes the existing declaration row to exact failed reads. Staging rows until accepted completion fixes never-accepted source attempts, and folds per-type references/struct references into NotedTypeDecl, removing two maps and duplicate events.

But /tmp/fz-tfn46-type-declaration-blocked-owner-red.log (2512, terminal failure) proves a real accepted-publication withdrawal hole: first global ScopeCode owns t=integer; later source has t=atom, require Range, then duplicate defstruct. Its real Blocked completion publishes t=atom. On resume it fails and withdraws its claim; the first publisher still claims TypeDeclared(t), but the visible row remains atom. This is a source value/claim coherence failure, not a speculative artifact claim. Earlier /tmp/fz-tfn46-type-declaration-shared-owner-red.log proved the never-accepted raw-row overwrite; staging now passes that control.

## Bounded strategy after confirmation
- Establish explicit source/publisher ownership at the existing declaration value authority before accepting a publication.
- Distinguish same-publisher reevaluation, competing new source declaration and explicit replacement; no last-writer-wins or arbitrary join among unequal declarations.
- Preserve exact prior value and provenance on rejected publication; withdrawal cannot leave another source's claim over the departing value.
- Keep declaration body and dependency references in one immutable publication snapshot; no rollback cache, parallel owner-value registry or retained staging bridge.
- Use existing scheduler-owned output frontiers and exact movements. Equal reproduction preserves allocation/generation and wakes nobody.
- Define the legitimate source-edit API/ownership prerequisite needed by repair tests; do not use the known duplicate-overwrite bug as proof of supported source replacement.
- Separate this work from eventual reclamation in fz-tfn.20. Re-evaluate dependencies on fz-kdt.24/.30 before implementation; do not silently absorb all source GC.

## Acceptance
Confirm the conflict policy first, then pin: duplicate same/different bodies according to that policy; same-owner equal and changed reevaluation; failed first publication; rejected publication with an existing owner; accepted Blocked publication followed by failure; exact last-owner withdrawal; protocol and macro-generated declarations; immutable diagnostic provenance; actual explicit replacement if needed by the adopted API. Use production boundaries and deterministic work/generation/allocation assertions. Preserve original healthy budgets/artifacts, delete superseded maps/events/adapters, update source/type docs, and cold-review the exact ticket before one commit/close.

## Execution boundary
No ownership winner policy or explicit replacement API is implemented yet. The .46 source candidate is preserved in the immutable parking boundary below; its independent interface-read corrections passed scoped review, but .46 cannot be accepted before this prerequisite. Root must preserve or explicitly park that candidate before isolating this ticket's implementation on the epic branch; do not blindly apply stashes or commit mixed tickets. Determine an atomic, buildable split from the existing candidate after the policy is confirmed. No source push or ticket close is authorized by this planning record alone.


## Current recoverable parking boundary
The complete fz-tfn.46 candidate remains preserved in immutable stash 710cba048553f39fbfcb4eb49171b92cdb7809f7, based on e616d82d13cc4e916bfae8e5a48e5219ac680d8a. Root previously verified every saved blob against its pre-stash SHA-256: 48 tracked files plus src/compiler2/failure.rs and .agent/measurements/fz-tfn46-validation.md in the stash third parent. Manifest SHA-256 efb787dc72ebd9b5f910722096863b8ca70915742cc687d1cb9836ae7c2f42ec. No stash has been dropped.

The accepted epic branch now includes fz-tfn.50, .55, .49 and .51; current head is 40563eeb756636153df0aac67d01940864fe2556. The .53 source-ownership policy remains unanswered, so .46 remains unaccepted and cannot close. Do not blindly restore .46 over the current branch. After policy confirmation, isolate the smallest atomic .53 value/owner cutover and reconcile the parked .46 candidate against the accepted current head, especially product_drive overlap. Earlier stash 288b and kdt46 stash 69e4 remain untouched.

Exact .51 own-head CI 34038513373 is active. Read-only research, paper contract and genuine RED construction may proceed, but no .53 successor push is allowed until that exact run is green.

## Current execution strategy
Use the semantic Output Contract Loop: state the externally visible duplicate/replacement contract, work the smallest two-source example on paper, expose the deciding owner/value fact at the production boundary, pin genuine RED before production, trace to the earliest incoherent value publication, then repair the data model and delete superseded stores/events/adapters. The implementation subagent may research current and parked source and propose the atomic split, but must not encode the still-unconfirmed conflict/replacement policy. Root owns bw/index/commit/close/push and independent proof.

## Completed read-only contract research

The ticket agent completed the paper contract without modifying source or running Cargo. The earliest incoherence is TypeDeclMap::note: the current scope walk mutates type references, struct references and the declaration as three independent TypeName stores, while the parked .46 candidate stages one immutable declaration snapshot but still writes its single value row before scheduler claim reconciliation. Several publishers can therefore claim TypeDeclared(name) while only the last value survives.

The smallest .53 cut is atomic owner/value publication at accepted job completion: validate the entire staged declaration batch before mutation; retain exact CodeId provenance; reject a distinct owner before it can alter the authoritative row or claim; allow an equal same-owner reevaluation to preserve generation and wake nobody; fold type and struct references into NotedTypeDecl; then delete TypeRefMap.by_type, by_type_structs and their adapters/events. CodeId provenance is required because Job identity does not distinguish competing sources that share DefineModule(ModuleId). No rollback map or parallel winner registry is permitted.

Protocol- and macro-generated declarations must retain their originating source CodeId; protocol-generated dummy spans are not sufficient provenance. The production work_graph.applied event and ordinary diagnostic telemetry are sufficient, so no redundant publication telemetry is needed.

Ticket fz-tfn.57 now records the independently required shared source-owner/version and all-output replacement boundary. It is intentionally not dependency-wired until the duplicate-type policy and atomic ordering are confirmed. Research found that a type-only replacement API is unsound: explicit replacement must transfer functions, modules, structs, macros, types, expectations, scheduler edges, diagnostics and retained products as one source operation. This is concordant with fz-kdt.24, fz-kdt.30, fz-kdt.32, fz-tfn.20, fz-tfn.40 and fz-tfn.45.

Open PR review found no semantic conflict: #110 is already incorporated; #111 has migration-wording and test-line drift in overlapping files; #113 only changes semantic-closure assertion wording. Reconcile textual drift when the chosen ticket lands.
title: Establish explicit source ownership for type declarations
